title: Oscar and the Promise
premise: Beatrix Dunmore built her career orchestrating other people's perfect days while quietly nursing a broken engagement she never mentions. When her grandmother's will stipulates that every Dunmore heir must arrive at the family reunion with a partner or forfeit their inheritance, Beatrix hires Oscar Reyes, the widowed florist whose flowers she orders for every wedding, to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. But the reunion stretches into a summer of staged dates, and the inheritance turns out to hinge on a secret: Grandmother's letter demands each heir prove they've chosen love over duty, not performed it. As Beatrix and Oscar's fake romance becomes indistinguishable from the real thing, an old betrayal surfaces that threatens both the fortune and their fragile trust. In the end, Beatrix must tear up the contract, confess everything to her family, and ask Oscar for one unscripted date — which he answers with a proposal of his own.
about_author: Wren Whitlock is the pen name of a former wedding coordinator who spent six years watching love get laminated into itineraries before escaping to write about the unscripted kind. They live in a coastal town full of hydrangeas and second chances, where they still can't resist eavesdropping on rehearsal dinners.

chapters.title: The Muscle Theory
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Opening on the flawless Hartwell wedding she produces, we learn her creed: hearts are trainable, containable — hers especially, since Daniel left her at the altar five years ago. A lawyer's letter arrives: Grandmother Eleanor's will requires all heirs to bring a partner to the Dunmore reunion or lose their share. Emotional beat: armored competence cracking under old grief.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She drafts a contract and takes it to Oscar Reyes, the gentle widowed florist who has supplied every wedding she's planned but never once flirted with her. He agrees — his flower shop is failing, and the fee would save it. They rehearse their meet-cute in his cooler among the peonies. Beat: transactional hope, both hiding how lonely they are.

chapters.title: Arrivals
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The reunion at Dunmore House begins; Oscar meets the sharp-tongued cousins, the disapproving uncle Marcus, and Beatrix's mother, who sees through nothing and everything. Their first improvised kiss on the terrace feels dangerously easy. Beat: the fake starts generating real heat neither planned for.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. At the welcome dinner, cousin Priya toasts 'the happy couple,' and Beatrix realizes she's laughing genuinely for the first time in years. Later, Oscar catches her crying over Eleanor's portrait and doesn't pry — he just sits with her. Beat: intimacy by accident; the lie deepens because the truth keeps leaking through.

chapters.title: The Letter Clause
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The lawyer reads Eleanor's codicil aloud: the inheritance goes only to heirs who can prove, by summer's end, that they chose love over duty — with evidence. Panic ripples through the family; suddenly everyone's romance is suspect, including theirs. Oscar realizes he's now complicit in fraud against a dead woman he'd have liked. Beat: stakes sharpened, guilt planted.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Real
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. To build 'evidence,' they stage dates — but a rainstorm strands them at a roadside diner where Oscar tells her about his late wife, Lena, and Beatrix almost tells him about Daniel. Instead she deflects with a joke, and he notices. Beat: the cost of containment made visible; first real rift of silence.

chapters.title: What Marcus Saw
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Uncle Marcus discovers the contract in Beatrix's bag and blackmails her: disqualify herself or he exposes the scheme to the whole family. Oscar overhears half the conversation and assumes Beatrix has been playing him for the money all along. Beat: miscommunication weaponized; loyalty and truth begin pulling apart.

chapters.title: Cold Flowers
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A week of frozen silences; Oscar returns the fee, Beatrix throws herself into a stranger's wedding and botches the toast. Her mother finally reveals Eleanor's own story: she gave up a true love for duty and regretted it for sixty years — the clause was her apology. Beat: despair before revelation; the theme lands.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Climax. At the final gathering, Marcus moves to expose her — and Beatrix stands first, confessing the contract, the fake dates, and then, voice breaking, the true part: she loves Oscar, duty be damned, and doesn't want a cent bought with a lie. Oscar arrives mid-confession, having driven through the night after finding her unsent letter. Beat: truth chosen over inheritance; public vulnerability as victory.

chapters.title: One Unscripted Date
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Resolution. The family, moved by Eleanor's letter, rewrites the will together; Beatrix walks away from her share to fund her own small planning studio — for people who want honest weddings. Oscar asks her on a date with no contract, no terms. She says yes before he finishes the sentence. Final image: peonies on her desk, unlabeled and free. Beat: whole heart risked, and kept.
